reviews.overall:
I checked 49 renders in C:\Users\danie\AppData\Roaming\Claude\scratch-workspaces\ec03f06b-60f5-4d5d-94a9-dff3a56c5f56\f8ddc2b6-f8a4-41c6-98db-14b97d4348ea\scratch-2026-09-23-d49817\renders2\review\ground\ and ran read-only Python on all 5,568 VK_ValleyTown objects (bound boxes and ray casts against a terrain BVH). Nothing in the scene was modified or saved.

Things that are fine:
- **Contact heights:** all nature, lip grass and seam rocks sit within 0.15 m of the surface (none float or sink). Building foundations follow their deliberate 0.6 m sink.
- **Terrain surface:** no holes or cracks are visible from above (a 0.3 m grid of ray casts hit terrain everywhere).
- **Water:** it covers every point below -0.65, so there are no dry pits.
- **Structures:** the stone bridge, the road ramps at rows 10 and 17, the sawpit and tanning pits, and the mine mound read fine.

The real problems, most severe first:
1. **Gate ramp:** the main-road ramp is 1.5 m off the gatehouse centre. It runs into the west tower, ends under the gate floor (a step of about 0.8 m), and leaves a 1.5 m drop at the east side of the passage.
2. **Footbridge:** it lands on sand strips enclosed by 1.5 m cliffs with no ramp or stair. The west road dead-ends at the cliff two cells away.
3. **Trees in the walls:** the scatter plants trees, bushes and flowers inside the town-wall masonry, and ridge pines grow through the north towers. Root cause: TownPlacer.P() never marks occupancy, so walls, towers, the gatehouse, the quay and bridges are invisible to town_scatter. The same cause puts 64 lip-grass tufts inside tower bases and a willow and reeds on the quay.
4. **Quarry:** it is a free-standing box with a 3 m trench between it and the ridge, and the crane sill overhangs the trench.
5. **Cliff-side props:** laundry line, fish rack, and the mill's cart and crates are jammed into the bank cliff.
6. **Smaller items:**
   - Dark skirts on the ramp sides.
   - Water cut open at the map edges, with displaced border vertices.
   - The smokehouse and mill corners sit on the bank crest.
   - Big trees stand at cliff toes.
   - The rowboat and barge clip the pier and quay stairs.
   - The barracks sits on the map edge.
   - The west stair is one cell off the road.
   - The river mouth has a boxy notch in the shore.

reviews.overall: Build/kit-integrity review of the VillageKit valley town. The scene was not modified or saved. VK_CamTmp was used for the renders, and temporary driver_namespace entries were removed afterwards. I rendered 39 views and read all of them (C:\Users\danie\AppData\Roaming\Claude\scratch-workspaces\ec03f06b-60f5-4d5d-94a9-dff3a56c5f56\f8ddc2b6-f8a4-41c6-98db-14b97d4348ea\scratch-2026-09-23-d49817\renders2\review\build\review_build_00..39*.png). I also ran read-only checks: mesh-level BVH overlaps between building pieces, town-wall pieces, props and trees; door-clearance tests along each door module's outward normal; terrain ray casts under ground-floor pieces; 1.5 m grid alignment; and a search for duplicate or coplanar wall modules. What is clean: there are no duplicate or coplanar (z-fighting) wall modules, no gaps in the town-wall runs, no infill houses overlapping each other, and ground floors sit flush on their cell level everywhere except intentional cases (granary on staddles, watermill pier, quay). The main defect is that town_walls places walls, towers and the gatehouse with T.P(), which never writes T.occ. As a result: (a) buildings in the first row inside the south wall (row 26) and the blacksmith (row 44) are built into the round towers and the gatehouse; (b) town_scatter plants trees and bushes inside the wall footprint on both sides; (c) the first infill house was placed into the gatehouse. Two further problems: the three west-quarter showcase buildings face their shopfronts toward the south wall, and several dressing props are placed in doorways, on the merchant yard's low wall, or through porch roofs. Registering the wall, tower and gatehouse footprints in T.occ, plus a door-clearance rule in the prop placer, would fix most of the list.

reviews.overall:
Art-direction review of the VillageKit scene, done read-only. Scene was not modified or saved. I rendered 31 views: 15 at the 40 m / 50° colony camera (including the overview), 12 at eye level and 3 at other angles and heights, plus one render (review_art_19) that I discarded because the camera was inside the granary. All are in C:\Users\danie\AppData\Roaming\Claude\scratch-workspaces\ec03f06b-60f5-4d5d-94a9-dff3a56c5f56\f8ddc2b6-f8a4-41c6-98db-14b97d4348ea\scratch-2026-09-23-d49817\renders2\review\art\ and I read every one. I also used read-only Python: a BVH of the terrain chunks, tree-versus-wall and tree-versus-tree bound-box and distance tests, and material and texture statistics.

What works: the hand-painted kit style reads clearly, especially the eye-level plaza and main street and the bridge, gate and windmill view (review_art_12, 13b, 23). Cobble, wall, plaster and roof-tile texel density is correct. Props sit on the ground properly: every flagged float or sink was intentional, such as foundation skirts, the saw pit, shop goods, bunting and boats on water.

Main art problems, most severe first:
1. Scattered trees are not culled against the town wall. 16 trees and bushes have trunks inside the wall footprint, so they grow out of the wall, including next to the gate.
2. Roofs are a saturated patchwork of orange-red, royal blue, green, slate and thatch, and roofs dominate the colony view.
3. Huge flat lawns in one saturated lime green (grass texture HSV saturation 0.70).
4. Water is emissive, milky turquoise and has no depth.
5. The willows are dark, hairy-looking domes, and one sits on the main road.
6. Scaffolding poles are white birch bark.
7. Roads look like brown carpet strips aligned to the cell grid.
8. The west-bench path misses its stair by one cell.
9. Some composition and readability issues: trees cover the camp, the lake cut at the map edge is visible, the forests are monotone and have duplicate trees, and some repetition and accent colours are too strong.

reviews.overall:
Play-lens review of the VillageKit valley map. I took 30 renders into C:/Users/danie/AppData/Roaming/Claude/scratch-workspaces/ec03f06b-60f5-4d5d-94a9-dff3a56c5f56/f8ddc2b6-f8a4-41c6-98db-14b97d4348ea/scratch-2026-09-23-d49817/renders2/review/play/ and read every one. I also ran a read-only pathing analysis. It rebuilt the level and water grid, which matched the terrain chunk BVH at all 4,032 cell centres. It cast a horizontal ray at 0.9 m (three lateral offsets) for every same-level cell edge, added the ramps, stairs and bridges from the grid, ran a BFS from the south road with and without passing through house doors, checked the front of all 52 door objects and every tower door, and looked for building and tower clashes. Nothing in the scene was modified and nothing was saved; the only temporary runtime data I made was the driver_namespace key _play_rev, which I removed again.

What works: the districts read well from the colony camera. The hamlet crop plots and pens, the meadow crafts (kiln, dye vats), the mine and quarry on the west bench, the chapel with its bell tower, and the plaza with its stalls and cross all read clearly. The stone bridge lines up with the road, and the town interior is fully connected.

The serious problems are about getting around:
- **Main gate:** it is off-centre from the road, so only one of the two road lanes gets through, and there is a lip mid-ramp at the threshold.
- **Wall towers:** four round towers are built into houses, and their ground doors are sealed.
- **Blocked doors:** props sit on the doorsteps of the barracks, blacksmith, brewery and a skyline house.
- **Footbridge:** it leads nowhere, because the banks at both ends have no ramps.
- **Unreachable spots:** the quarry crane stands on an unreachable level-4 ledge, the merchant house's stair yard is sealed, and willow trees block the only way to the fisher hut, the quay and the bridge approach.

Two layout issues follow from having a single gate in the south: the west-bench industries are about 170 m away by path, and the main shops face the town wall.
